author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Keep a read-only PS2 preservation master and a separate working copy
summary: Freeze a verified personal dump with logs and hashes outside EmuCoreX scans, derive a replaceable working copy for names and external patches, and rehearse rebuilding that copy without modifying the master.
heroAlt: Media Preservation Frontend download screen representing the controlled tooling used to create a preservation master

blocks.text: Give the master and working copy different permissions and locations

The preservation master represents what was read from an owned disc. It retains original tool names, cue/bin structure, dump logs, hashes, and source notes. The working copy is what EmuCoreX scans and what the owner may rename or pair with external patches. Keeping them in separate roots prevents a library cleanup or experiment from rewriting the recovery source.

Read-only is not a backup. Keep another verified master copy on a separate physical device, and never expose either master through a folder granted to patching or synchronization tools that can rewrite it.

items: Two matching personal disc reads or equivalent verified preservation result.
All dump logs and CD cue/bin components retained.
SHA-256 manifest covering every master file.
A private master directory outside EmuCoreX library roots.
A second independent storage device for recovery redundancy.

blocks.text: Derive and validate the playable branch

items: 1. Mark the verified master directory read-only using the storage system's supported permissions or physical workflow.
2. Copy the complete image set into an empty working directory and record its origin manifest.
3. Compare working hashes with the master before any rename or external patch configuration.
4. Rename only the working files, updating cue references where necessary.
5. Point EmuCoreX at the working root and cold-boot at Safe defaults.
6. Apply enhancements externally where supported so the original image bytes stay identifiable.
7. After deliberate working changes, record new derived hashes and the patch or rename instructions.
8. Rebuild one working copy from the master as a rehearsal, proving recovery does not depend on memory.

blocks.text: A patched image is a derived artifact and must never inherit the label master. When storage is limited, the active working copy can be replaced from the master, but the private preservation record should remain stable. Backups can be compressed after verification as long as test extraction reproduces every master hash.
The two branches should be distinguishable by path, permissions, manifest, and purpose.

items: Master hashes equal the verified dump record.
EmuCoreX scans only the working root.
Working copy begins byte-identical before documented derivations.
Master directory timestamps and hashes remain unchanged after experiments.
A fresh working copy can be reconstructed and cold-booted.

blocks.text: Boundary failures that end the experiment

items: Master hash changes: stop and restore from the independent verified backup.
EmuCoreX shows master and working entries: remove the master root grant.
Cue working copy loses audio: restore the complete set and update references correctly.
Patch instructions cannot reproduce the derived state: discard the working branch and document the gap.

blocks.text: Regenerate instead of repairing unknown bytes

Remove the damaged working set from the active root, copy a new complete set from the verified master, compare hashes, restore only documented names and external enhancements, then refresh once. Never copy uncertain working bytes back into the master directory.
Private firmware and disc data stay private
Manifests, serials, logs, and hashes can describe a workflow, but the Hub repository and support reports must not contain BIOS files, game images, keys, or copyrighted disc contents.
